remaining: Actual host pause/cancel, transfer/timezone, staged FileProvider writeback, supervision/admin/deadline/pressure/shutdown
Two actual io_uring source-maintenance failure escalations and known unsupported resources/subcommands
limits: No new resource/coordinator thread: native output uses the same existing file/image pool. Nonblocking host input remains on the host callback thread.
Already accepted native OS writes still finish during pool teardown; arbitrary blocked OS calls are not cancellable.
No connected transport adds a new scheduler poll deadline; embedding terminal transport retains a 2 ms host poll bound.
Terminal query timings are subsystem measurements, not Firefox/Geekbench scores. Native Darwin/Linux tty semantics and scheduler/filesystem backing differ.
Native Linux controls ran in the existing six-vCPU ARM64 local CI instance; it was stopped for paired HVF timing.

The initial duplex fixture failed to limit its last write after short writes, causing excess output. The fixture was corrected and rerun; obsolete multi-GB output was discarded. No production failure was inferred from that fixture error.
Initial process failures included sandbox-denied loopback sockets and an old test-only external-input declaration. Final full runs pass on both hosts.
The short one-CPU query fixture varies between initial and final paired sets; this is evidence of no observed regression, not a claimed general CPU speedup.
